Hi Sofia / Redwood finance team,

We're reconciling the Dec 15 settlement and our bank reports show a EUR remittance that doesn't match the USD AR application you have on your portal. Attached is our remittance file (BRIGHTGRID_remit_20261215.csv) and a short reconciliation showing the EUR->USD conversion and the settlement reference.

We need confirmation by end-of-week so our month-end closes clean.

Thanks,

Sofia / Marcus / Anna (cc'd),

I pulled the posting in our ledger and here's the short version: the EUR remittance (EUR 42,300) was auto-applied by the payment gateway to the US AR entity (Redwood Inc.) on Dec 15, using the payment flow mapping default. The invoice (BG-INV-99241) is billed to Redwood EU Ltd., so the AR balance for EU remains open while the US AR shows a foreign-currency credit. That produced an unapplied payment balance in account 1310_SUSPENSE and an FX variance of USD 1,120 (gain) sitting in 6700_FX_DIFF.

Proposal (cleanest operational path):
1) Create intercompany JE to move EUR 42,300 from 1310_SUSPENSE (Redwood Inc.) to 1100_AR (Redwood EU Ltd.) at the bank-converted USD value posted by the gateway (USD 44,520).
2) Post a separate FX adjustment JE to move USD 1,120 from 6700_FX_DIFF to 4100_OTHER_INCOME (or to an 'FX clearing' suspense if tax requires).
3) Add a memo referencing BrightGrid remittance and BG-INV-99241.

I attached an apply matrix for the payment routing and a draft journal template (journal_proposal_q4.xlsx). If leadership approves, Accounting Ops can post JE and then we notify BrightGrid with the corrected application.

Attachments: apply_matrix_DEC2026.csv; journal_proposal_q4.xlsx

Numbers: EUR 42,300 -> USD 44,520 (gateway rate used 1.0539). FX variance recorded as USD 1,120.

Let me know if you want me to draft the JE in the system and assign to Laura for posting.

—Grace O'Connor
Senior AR Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks Grace — that approach looks operationally sensible. A couple of flags from my side:
- We need to ensure VAT/tax coding follows the EU entity mapping. If we move the AR to Redwood EU Ltd., VAT reporting could change if the original invoice tax code was incorrectly applied during the gateway auto-apply.
- Please confirm whether the original invoice included VAT (I believe BG-INV-99241 is a B2B EU supply with 0% VAT but I want the tax team to confirm).

Rishi: can you confirm whether this reposting and the FX reclassification requires any additional documentation for VAT reclaim or adjustments in the EU VAT filing? If yes, we should attach the payment receipt and the remittance trace in the JE comments.

Marcus Lin
Director, Revenue Accounting

Team,

Checked the tax angles. Confirmations:
- BG-INV-99241 is B2B EU supply and was raised net of VAT (0%). Moving the AR to the EU entity will not change the VAT treatment for the invoice itself.
- The FX variance is an accounting item and should not affect VAT reclaim. However, we must maintain clear audit trails: remittance file, payment gateway allocation record, and the JE memo.

Request: please include the BrightGrid remittance CSV and the AR portal extract in the JE attachments. Also tag the JE with tax code EU-0 so Tax can pick it up in the quarterly file.

I approve the two-step JE as drafted; Finance leadership approval is still required to post.
